newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Prague PSE members to trade only on organised markets.
newsitem.headline: Prague PSE members to trade only on organised markets.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) governing board has agreed to force its members to trade only on organised markets, thus eliminating their ability to make over-the-counter trades simply recorded at the Central Securities Registry (SCP).
"Members of the bourse must trade in securities only on organised markets," PSE Chamber chairman Tomas Jezek told a news conference on Tuesday, saying the rule would take effect on August 1.
The rule would allow PSE members, numbering more than 100 firms, to conduct trades through the retail-oriented bourse, RM-System.
The PSE has been taking steps to concentrate more trading on its central market and limit the OTC trades which still dominate turnover in Czech securities.
Czech OTC trades have been frequently criticised for questionable pricing methods and poor transparency, while activity on Prague's two organised markets has remained relatively thin.

The chamber agreed that fees for direct trades registered at the Prague Stock Exchange would be proportional to total turnover and no longer a simple flat fee, and transaction fees for trades on the central market would be lowered, Jezek said.
"The impact of the change has the character of strengthening the central price-making market," Jezek added.
